core_summary: The Earth, Moon, and Sun form an interconnected celestial system governing day/night cycles, seasons, lunar phases, and eclipses. Earth rotates on its 23.5-degree tilted axis every 24 hours (causing day and night) and revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit every 365.25 days (causing seasons). The Moon orbits Earth every 29.5 days, displaying changing lunar phases from New Moon (Amavasya) to Full Moon (Purnima). Eclipses occur during exact linear alignments: Solar Eclipse on New Moon (Moon between Sun and Earth); Lunar Eclipse on Full Moon (Earth between Sun and Moon). Indian observatories like IIA and ARIES contribute astronomical data.
key_concepts: To model solar and lunar eclipse shadow geometries using a torch and spheres.

key_terms.definition: Sun --- Moon --- Earth (Moon obstructs solar light).
Sun --- Earth --- Moon (Earth obstructs light reaching Moon).

key_takeaways: Seasons are caused by Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt during revolution, changing angle and duration of sunlight, NOT by distance variation from the Sun.
